He knows exactly how to create the finest flavors.
Isabela Maranta, The Queen of Pineapples
A passionate grower of the Caribbean, her golden fruits are the pride of the tropics and the desire of distant ports.
Don Everardo Gómez, The Compost Master
With his ancestral wisdom and modern precision, he transforms manure and minerals into the secret of tropical agricultural success.
Doña Caridad Herrera, The Lady of Sweet Gold
With a steady gaze and neat hands, she oversees each box of pineapples as if it were a treasure about to cross the sea.
She knows each herb by its feel and aroma; its drying transforms simple leaves into herbal teas of character and depth.
Janneke van Hout, The Clog Master
Born among shavings and fine woods, Janneke carves each pair as if it were a work of art for the feet of the people.

A meticulous botanist with a fondness for anything that burns—on the tongue, that is. Habelwurz spent years crossbreeding wild Brassicaceae species and developed an especially high-yield mustard seed variety known as "Habelgold." His methods are controversial, but the yields speak for themselves.

“You must read the sea like an old journal.” A silent northerner with steady hands and decades of experience. Fluefisker doesn’t fish—he composes. His lines move like whispers through icy waters, and his techniques are as graceful as they are deadly. Since retiring from the royal polar expedition, he keeps to himself, but his knowledge of fish routes and seal migration is unmatched.
Brunhilde Senftreu, purveyor to the court of the ducal mustard office

“Only the finest grind shall grace the noble table.” With roots in an old family of condiment artisans, Brunhilde Senftreu rose through the ranks of the courtly kitchens to become the official mustard purveyor of the ducal household. Fiercely committed to tradition and quality, she oversees every batch with a silver ladle and a critical eye. Her presence alone inspires workers to stir a little faster and press a little harder.
Da Huaba Sepp, the master of meat

“If it ain’t juicy, it ain’t worth chewing.” A living Bavarian cliché with a proud belly, bristly moustache, and a love for all things ground, baked, and pork-based. Sepp—known as "Da Huaba"—has elevated meatloaf (or Leberkäse) into a culinary art. With well-guarded spice blends and a smoker’s instinct, his loaves bring joy to the masses—and cholesterol to the nobility.
Deorges Gelbard, the Rose Virtuoso of Chartres

“Every rose is a poem—but only the right one blooms in time.” Gelbard is no mere gardener; he is a rose-whisperer with silk gloves and iron resolve. Raised among the greenhouses of the Loire, he breeds blooms that open to the morning sun and release fragrance to the sound of string quartets. His cultivars grace royal gardens and fine perfume bottles alike—he gave the rose its dignity back.

“It ain’t real smoke if it don’t sting your eyes a bit.” Grumbly, proud, and with a pipe that’s been lit longer than most factories have stood—Holmy is a legend in smokehouses across the north. A retired sailor turned smoker of fine fish, he knows every trick of the trade, from alderwood blends to the perfect brine. His smoked salmon is worth its salt—and then some.

“A single drop can awaken memories, or ruin a royal dessert.” Renowned across the Levant and beyond, Nuri is not merely a distiller—he is a perfumer of purpose, a chemist of the sublime. His rosewater is more than an extract: it’s an experience. Using copper stills and secret blends of damask petals, he produces liquid elegance drop by drop. Nobles compete for his flacons; workers, for his methods.
Radi-Rudi, cuts quicker than his shadow

“Blink and your cabbage is coleslaw.” A whirlwind with a cleaver and a legend in local markets, Radi-Rudi gained fame for his knife skills, slicing roots, leaves, and even paperwork with breathtaking precision. No one knows his real name—or how many fingers he has left. What’s certain: production speeds up wherever he goes.
Sebald Salzkringel, the cake is a lye

“The secret’s in the lye. And in the twist of the wrist.” A crusty old soul with flour in his veins and salt on the brain, Sebald doesn’t just bake pretzels—he lives them. His twisted creations are a blend of tradition, technique, and spiritual devotion. No one braids dough like him, and no oven ever dares burn his batch. Bakers speak of him in hushed, yeasty reverence.
Clémence Van der Noot, Chocolate is Love
A master chocolatier from Brussels, her pralines and marzipan recipes seduce palates from kings to farmers.

With endless patience and a genuine affection for all living creatures, Robrecht Veldsteen understands animals better than people. To prevent needless slaughter, he replaces meat with potatoes in everyday recipes, proving that prosperity does not always demand blood.
Amir al-Tamr, keeper of the golden dates

“Patience is the sun beneath which the sweetest fruits ripen.” Descended from a lineage of oasis gardeners, Amir al-Tamr has spent his life perfecting the art of date cultivation. He knows the breath of the desert wind, when the sand grows weary, and when the fruit whispers readiness. Under his care, even the driest palms bear abundance. His dates are famed for their golden hue and honeyed taste—a gift of the desert sun.
Don Pascual Piñaverti, the pineapple alchemist

“Why distill hardship when one can bottle sunshine?” Born among tropical breezes and fruit markets, Pascual Piñaverti believes the world has underestimated the humble pineapple. He revolutionized distilleries by replacing sugarcane and potatoes with golden fruit, creating spirits that taste like summer and rebellion. Some say he’s mad, some say he’s ahead of his time. He says: “Try one sip.”
Gregor von Schallheim, Lord Commander of the Crown’s Airships

Born into a lineage linked to the royal house, he was destined from childhood to elevate the monarchy's ambitions to new heights. With unwavering loyalty and a seaman's instinct honed by generations past, he became the first to chart the course for the royal airship fleet.
A veteran of markets, caravans and ports, Basilio masters the art of supplying entire cities without wasting a single gram of food.
